createModal.title: Create New Domain
createModal.subtitle: The Linux user, nginx vhost, PHP-FPM pool, FTP account, MySQL database, and DNS zone are configured automatically.
createModal.domainNameHintPre: Lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens, and periods. For example:

siteTypeHints.php: A MySQL database is created. For Laravel, Symfony and other PHP applications.

siteTypeHints.static: No database is created. For HTML, CSS and JavaScript only.

createModal.ownerHint: Pick the reseller the domain belongs to, then one of its customers. Leave both as they are to keep the domain under the administrator.
createModal.issueSsl: Install a Let's Encrypt SSL certificate after creation
createModal.sslWarning: ⚠️ The domain's DNS A record must already point to this server, otherwise issuance fails and you can retry later from the SSL page.

stages.domain: Creating the domain and its accounts

resultModal.title: ✓ Domain Created
resultModal.readyPre: is ready. The passwords below are shown
resultModal.ownerNotApplied: The domain was created, but the reseller you picked was not applied: this system user already has a customer record, and an existing record keeps the owner it had. Use the owner change action to move it.
resultModal.sslNote: The certificate is being issued in the background and can take several minutes. Progress and the result, including a fall back to a self-signed certificate, are on the SSL page.
resultModal.wordpressNote: The install needs a site title, an administrator name and an email address, so it is not run automatically.
resultModal.nameserversNote: Change the nameservers at the domain's registrar to these values. Propagation takes 1 to 24 hours; after that every DNS record is managed from the panel.
